structuredOutput.summary: Add a pure v2 private-backup HTTP boundary in two new files. createPrivateBackupV2Api mirrors the v1 fail-closed host style while preserving the existing v2 client route/request contract: session auth stays on the HTTP host, raw body caps stay on the caller, download token consumption/streaming stay on the coordinator, and this layer never touches disk, network, keys, or workspace selection. Service methods are invoked only after strict input checks; every success projection is revalidated with the shared parsers (id/kind included) so unknown private fields cannot be stripped into a 200/202.
risks: HTTP host must apply session protection before this function; the boundary does not authenticate or authorize.
Caller must cap raw request reads at 1MiB before allocating bytes; this layer only rejects an already-allocated buffer.
Service exceptions propagate with original messages. Root HTTP must map them to safe client bodies or internals leak.
GET /downloads only returns a token. Coordinator must consume the ticket and stream; this module never opens files or builds disk paths.
Invalid UUID/token path segments are unmatched 404s, not 400s. Uppercase UUIDs will 404 because shared ids are lowercase hex.
BackupV2ApiService positional signatures must stay locked with Codex wiring and the storage proposal; this file does not implement transfer/storage.
Tests use node:test. If the repo runner is vitest-only, the new test file needs the same runner as sibling server tests.
Invalid service projections throw 500 with the public storage-unavailable copy, which can look like a real storage failure in logs.
